summary: Thursday 19 Nov. Themes: coffee and sleep (genes and caffeine clearance), coffee and the gut microbiome for Mornings, FSSAI's 16 Nov action against six nutraceutical makers, the Instagram skip list carried to X, and a mouse study on fibre and the gut lining. No LinkedIn (Thursday) and no poll. Reddit is blocked for Claude, so there are 8 bank comments on coffee and the toilet, 3 AM waking, ashwagandha doses, sugar cravings, caffeine and L-theanine ratios, office breakfasts, first 100 customers and phone scrolling in bed.

trends.topic: Genes may shape coffee's link to Parkinson's risk; benefit seen mainly in fast caffeine metabolisers (UK Biobank, observational)
trends.angle: Nights: caffeine lingers, so time your last cup

trends.topic: Coffee drinkers had more gut microbial diversity and lower small-intestine pH (University of Copenhagen)
trends.angle: Mornings: caffeine plus gut, with the no-cause caveat

trends.topic: FSSAI action against six nutraceutical manufacturers, 16 Nov (expired materials, thiamin above the daily reference, labelling)
trends.angle: Transparency: 100% RDA and per-ingredient lab reports

trends.topic: Mouse study (PNAS): fibre-starved gut bacteria feed on the mucus lining
trends.angle: Education: mechanism, not proof in people

trends.topic: Coffee 2 to 3 cups a day linked to lower dementia risk; decaf showed no comparable link (JAMA, observational)
trends.angle: Held back to avoid a third coffee post. Usable later as an education post

trends.topic: Fibre blend (resistant starch plus psyllium) improved gut measures in IBS without worsening symptoms (Eur J Nutr, Edith Cowan)
trends.angle: Backlog for a fibre education post; avoid any IBS treatment claim for PHGG

trends.topic: Indian IT staff pushing back on late-night US meetings, right to disconnect
trends.angle: Already used (late US calls). Save for a Friday LinkedIn angle later

trends.topic: L-theanine 31-trial meta-analysis (reported as Molecular Psychiatry 2026): modest acute stress effect
trends.angle: NOT USED: only found on secondary and vendor sites, primary paper not verified
